```{r, Loading libraries}

library(EnhancedVolcano) #volcano plots
```

```{r, Reading the gene count matrix CSV into the document}

#The gene count matrix csv file loaded into r
count_matrix_2026 <- read.csv("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/Expression_Quantification/gene_count_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)

#Also the csv file loaded into r, but I will use this copy to make it so that ONLY ensembl ids appear as rownames
count_matrix_2026_idsonly <- read.csv("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/Expression_Quantification/gene_count_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)

```

```{r, Creating count_matrix_2026_idsonly, which has just ensembl ids in rownames}

#Creating data frame with count_matrix rownames
ensembl_ids2026 <- data.frame(rownames(count_matrix_2026))

#Gets rid of the gene symbols by removing everything after the | symbol. 
ensembl_ids2026$rownames <- sub("\\|.*", "", ensembl_ids2026$rownames.count_matrix_2026.)

#Replaces row names in the count_matrix_2026_idsonly file with ensembl ids
if (length(ensembl_ids2026$rownames) == nrow(count_matrix_2026_idsonly)) {
  rownames(count_matrix_2026_idsonly) <- ensembl_ids2026$rownames
} else {
  stop("The length of the new gene names does not match the number of rows in the count matrix.")
}
```

```{r, Getting gene symbols for ensembl ids and chromosomes for respective genes from biomart}
******************
#This creates a data set with all the chicken info from ensembl summoned by biomart. The host is specified so it runs when the main website is down. The version is specified because that's the version the original alignment was done with, and newer versions don't work.
ensembl <- useEnsembl(biomart = "genes", dataset = "ggallus_gene_ensembl", mirror = "www", host = "https://jun2026.archive.ensembl.org", version = 106)

#Searches the datasets available on biomart for a key term, in this case looking for chicken genome
searchDatasets(mart = ensembl, pattern = "ggallus")

#Once we've found the dataset we need we can specify this for biomart
ensembl <- useDataset(dataset = "ggallus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl)

#Searches the attributes available on biomart for a key term, we would like the gene symbol
searchAttributes(mart = ensembl, pattern = "symbol")

#You have to run this twice don't ask me why
ensembl <- useEnsembl(biomart = "genes", dataset = "ggallus_gene_ensembl", host = "https://useast.ensembl.org")

#Creates data frame with ensembl ids, corresponding gene symbols from uniprot_gn_symbol, and the chromosome each gene is on
mart_result <- getBM(mart = ensembl, attributes = c("chromosome_name", "uniprot_gn_symbol", "ensembl_gene_id"), filters = "ensembl_gene_id", values = ensembl_ids2026$rownames)

mart_result$symbols_ids <- make.unique(mart_result$symbols_ids)

```

```{r, Assigning gene symbols and ensembl ids to count_matrix_2026_symbid}

#Need to insert NA's into the blank spots of the mart_result data frame for the following code to work
mart_result[mart_result == ""] <- NA
#Creating column with both symbols and IDs in the mart_result data frame (for genes without symbols, there will be IDs)
mart_result$symbols_ids <- ifelse(
  is.na(mart_result$uniprot_gn_symbol),
  mart_result$ensembl_gene_id,
  mart_result$uniprot_gn_symbol)

#Save the mart_result as a tsv for later use in WGCNA
write.table(mart_result,"~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/mart_result.tsv")

#Turning the rownames of the count_matrix_2025_idsonly into a column
count_matrix_2026_idsonly <- tibble::rownames_to_column(count_matrix_2026_idsonly, "ensembl_gene_id")

#Merging the count_matrixids only with the mart_result by the ensembl ids and creating the count_matrix_2025_symbid data frame
count_matrix_2026_symbid <- merge(count_matrix_2026_idsonly, mart_result, by = "ensembl_gene_id")

#Makes all of the columns in the symbols_ids unique by adding .1, .2, etc so that it can be converted to rownames
count_matrix_2026_symbid$symbols_ids <- make.unique(count_matrix_2026_symbid$symbols_ids)

#Converting the symbols_ids column to rownames
count_matrix_2026_symbid <- tibble::column_to_rownames(count_matrix_2026_symbid,"symbols_ids")

#Making a copy of the count_matrix with the extra information to use for other analysis
count_matrix_2026_symbid_copy <- count_matrix_2026_symbid
#Deleting the extra columns so that this count matrix can be used for DESeq
count_matrix_2026_symbid$ensembl_gene_id <- NULL
count_matrix_2026_symbid$chromosome_name <- NULL
count_matrix_2026_symbid$uniprot_gn_symbol <- NULL
```

```{r, Reading in the Phenodata csv file}

#The phenodata file containing meta data on samples for differential gene expression purposes
#Running with sample 9 switched to Saline-ZW
chicken_phenodata <- read.csv("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/ChickenPhenodata_9ZW_2026.csv", sep = ";")

#Sets the sample names to row names to make it easier to run following checks
chicken_phenodata <- tibble::column_to_rownames(chicken_phenodata, "sample")

##Checks to make sure deseq can run and the row names are sample IDs matching those of the columns from the count_matrix:
#Row names of count matrix match column names of sample file?
all(colnames(count_matrix_2026_symbid) %in% rownames(chicken_phenodata))
#In the same order?
all(colnames(count_matrix_2026_symbid) == rownames(chicken_phenodata))

#Re-leveling the data, like setting 'controls' of a sort, to be used in DESEQ later
chicken_phenodata$Treatment <- factor(chicken_phenodata$Treatment, levels = c("Saline", "Fadrozole"))
chicken_phenodata$Chromosome <- factor(chicken_phenodata$Chromosome, levels = c("ZZ", "ZW"))
```

```{r, Creating the DESeq2 dataset object}

#Creating dds object with design meant to capture interaction between chromosome and treatment
dds2026_data = DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = count_matrix_2026_symbid, #1
                       colData = chicken_phenodata, #2
                       design = ~ Chromosome+Treatment + Chromosome:Treatment) #3

#1: Tells R what matrix to draw gene expression data from
#2: Tells R what data frame to use as the colData, or metadata file, creating subgroups of the columns to compare gene expression between
#3: This design should look at a the overall differential expression based on chromosome type, treatment type, and whether or not there is an interaction between the two independent variables

#Checking that factor levels are correct
levels(dds2026_data$Treatment)
levels(dds2026_data$Chromosome)

#Running DESeq
dds2026 <- DESeq(dds2026_data)

```
```{r, Contrasts}

#Looks at the names of the available contrasts created by the DESeq design
resultsNames(dds2026)

##Main effect of chromosome in saline group

res_chro_sal <- data.frame(results(dds2026, contrast = list("Chromosome_ZW_vs_ZZ")))
#Sorting out genes differentially expressed with p value less than 0.01
res_chro_salsig <- as.data.frame(res_chro_sal[!is.na(res_chro_sal$pvalue) & res_chro_sal$pvalue < 0.01,])
#Creating table with significant genes and their chromosome
res_chro_salsig <- tibble::rownames_to_column(res_chro_salsig, "symbols_ids")
res_chro_salsig <- merge(res_chro_salsig, mart_result, by = "symbols_ids")
#Saving as csv to open in excel
write.csv(res_chro_salsig, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/DGE_Results_2026/res_chro_salsig.csv", row.names = FALSE)


##Main effect of chromosome in fadrozole group

res_chro_fad <- data.frame(results(dds2026, contrast = list("Chromosome_ZW_vs_ZZ", "ChromosomeZW.TreatmentFadrozole")))
#Sorting out genes differentially expressed with p value less than 0.01
res_chro_fadsig <- as.data.frame(res_chro_fad[!is.na(res_chro_fad$pvalue) & res_chro_fad$pvalue < 0.01,])
#Creating table with significant genes and their chromosome
res_chro_fadsig <- tibble::rownames_to_column(res_chro_fadsig, "symbols_ids")
res_chro_fadsig <- merge(res_chro_fadsig, mart_result, by = "symbols_ids")
#Saving as csv to open in excel
write.csv(res_chro_fadsig, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/DGE_Results_2026/res_chro_fadsig.csv", row.names = FALSE)


##Main effect of treatment in ZZ

res_treat_zz <- data.frame(results(dds2026, contrast = list("Treatment_Fadrozole_vs_Saline")))
#Sorting out genes differentially expressed with p value less than 0.01
res_treat_zzsig <- as.data.frame(res_treat_zz[!is.na(res_treat_zz$pvalue) & res_treat_zz$pvalue < 0.01,])
#Creating table with significant genes and their chromosome
res_treat_zzsig <- tibble::rownames_to_column(res_treat_zzsig, "symbols_ids")
res_treat_zzsig <- merge(res_treat_zzsig, mart_result, by = "symbols_ids")
#Saving as csv to open in excel
write.csv(res_treat_zzsig, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/DGE_Results_2026/res_treat_zzsig.csv", row.names = FALSE)


##Main effect of treatment in ZW

res_treat_zw <- data.frame(results(dds2026, contrast = list("Treatment_Fadrozole_vs_Saline", "ChromosomeZW.TreatmentFadrozole")))
#Sorting out genes differentially expressed with p value less than 0.01
res_treat_zwsig <- as.data.frame(res_treat_zw[!is.na(res_treat_zw$pvalue) & res_treat_zw$pvalue < 0.01,])
#Creating table with significant genes and their chromosome
res_treat_zwsig <- tibble::rownames_to_column(res_treat_zwsig, "symbols_ids")
res_treat_zwsig <- merge(res_treat_zwsig, mart_result, by = "symbols_ids")
#Saving as csv to open in excel
write.csv(res_treat_zwsig, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/DGE_Results_2026/res_treat_zwsig.csv", row.names = FALSE)


##Interaction

res_int <- data.frame(results(dds2026, contrast = list("ChromosomeZW.TreatmentFadrozole")))
#Sorting out genes differentially expressed with p value less than 0.01
res_intsig <- as.data.frame(res_int[!is.na(res_int$pvalue) & res_int$pvalue < 0.01,])
#Creating table with significant genes and their chromosome
res_intsig <- tibble::rownames_to_column(res_intsig, "symbols_ids")
res_intsig <- merge(res_intsig, mart_result, by = "symbols_ids")
#Saving as csv to open in excel
write.csv(res_intsig, "~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/DGE_Results_2026/res_intsig.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r, PCA Plot 2026}

#Creating PCA Object
pca2026 = vst(dds2025, blind=FALSE)

pca_data2026 <- plotPCA(pca2026, intgroup=c("Chromosome", "Treatment", "Chromosome_Treatment"), returnData=TRUE)

#Calc percent variance
percent_var2026 <- round(100*attr(pca_data2026,"percentVar"))

#Constructing plot 
pca_plot <- ggplot(pca_data2026, aes(PC1, PC2))+
  geom_point(size=4, aes(col=Chromosome_Treatment))+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("#0D0887FF","#B12A90FF", "#E16462FF","#FCA636FF"))+
  theme_classic() + theme(
    legend.position = "none", 
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"))+ coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-15, 30)) # Sets x-axis from 2 to 5

#Save PCA plot as a PDF for import into illustrator
pdf("~/Workspace/BIO-BIRDLAB/Shared/Chicken_Project/PCA_Plot/PCAplot2026_2.pdf", width = 2.5, height = 2.5)
par(mar = c(4, 4, 4, 4))
pca_plot + #ggtitle("Principal Component Analysis (PCA) plot of 4 groups") + 
  xlab("Feature 1") +
  ylab("Feature 2")
dev.off()
```

```{r, Volcano Plots}
###Making volcano plots showing the log fold change and significance of differentially expressed genes between main four contrasts

##res_chro_sal

#Make a copy of the results table
copy_res_chro_sal <- res_chro_sal

#Add a column to specify significant UP/DOWN regulation
copy_res_chro_sal$diffexpressed <- "Non-signficiant"
copy_res_chro_sal$diffexpressed[copy_res_chro_sal$log2FoldChange > 0.2 & copy_res_chro_sal$pvalue < 0.01] <- "UP"
copy_res_chro_sal$diffexpressed[copy_res_chro_sal$log2FoldChange < -0.2 & copy_res_chro_sal$pvalue < 0.01] <- "DOWN"

#Create volcano plot
vol_chrosal <- ggplot(data = copy_res_chro_sal, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue), col = diffexpressed)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.2, 0.2), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') + #the vertical intercept line
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(.01), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') + #the horizontal intercept line
  geom_point(size = 2,  alpha = 0.5) + #the points
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#1F1BB3", "gray", "#D41159"))+ #the colors of the points
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 70), xlim = c(-45, 45)) + #the plot/axis dimensions
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 70, 20)) + #y axis numbers
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"))

##res_chro_fad

#Make a copy of the results table
copy_res_chro_fad <- res_chro_fad

#Add a column to specify UP/DOWN regulation
copy_res_chro_fad$diffexpressed <- "Non-signficiant"
copy_res_chro_fad$diffexpressed[copy_res_chro_fad$log2FoldChange > 0.2 & copy_res_chro_fad$pvalue < 0.01] <- "UP"
copy_res_chro_fad$diffexpressed[copy_res_chro_fad$log2FoldChange < -0.2 & copy_res_chro_fad$pvalue < 0.01] <- "DOWN"

#Create volcano plot
vol_chrofad <- ggplot(data = copy_res_chro_fad, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue), col = diffexpressed)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.2, 0.2), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(.01), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_point(size = 2,  alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#1F1BB3", "gray", "#D41159")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 70), xlim = c(-45, 45)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-40, 40, 20)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 70, 20))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"), axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), #remove axis text,
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank() #remove axis ticks
  )

##res_treat_zz

#Make a copy of the results table
copy_res_treat_zz <- res_treat_zz

#Add a column to specify UP/DOWN regulation
copy_res_treat_zz$diffexpressed <- "Non-signficiant"
```

```{r, WGCNA preperation}

#Enable multi-threading for WGCNA (adjust based on your system)
enableWGCNAThreads(nThreads = 8)

#Normalization 

#Using the deseq dataset already created to use the deseq package normalization function
dds2026_data[rowSums(counts(dds2026_data)>=15)>=24]
#Variacne stablization
dds_norm <- vst(dds2026_data)
#Normalized Counts
norm_counts <- assay(dds_norm)
norm_counts <- as.data.frame(norm_counts)
norm_counts <- tibble::rownames_to_column(norm_counts, "Genes")
#Save as a csv for import into WGCNA R mark down file
write.table(norm_counts, file = "normalized_counts.csv", sep = ",", col.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)

```
